title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Scammers used deepfakes and voice-cloning technology to impersonate an immigration attorney in South Florida, targeting immigrants seeking legal help. The impersonation was not caught before victims sent money, because the system—a social engineering fraud—had no gatekeeper. Deepfake and voice-cloning systems exist to create convincing forgeries; no technical control was present between their output and the victims who encountered them.

The failure was one of identity verification at the point of service delivery. Someone claiming to be a licensed attorney offered legal services without any mechanism to confirm their license, credentials, or identity. A victim could have verified the attorney's identity through official bar records or by calling the attorney's known office, but no system required this step before payment.

Whether the AI systems themselves were built for this use is not established. The systems appear to have been deployed by scammers for impersonation, not by the attorney or any legitimate legal service provider.

summary:
# Summary

Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to commit fraud across Georgia and South Florida by creating deepfakes and cloned voices to impersonate trusted individuals. A South Florida immigration attorney had his voice and identity stolen to target immigrants seeking legal help, while a Cobb County couple lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in losses from AI-enabled scams in the past year as criminals grew more sophisticated in their techniques.

The problem is particularly prevalent in Florida, which saw 350 AI-related complaints resulting in $39.9 million in losses, and Georgia, with 71 complaints totaling over $10.4 million in losses. Scammers use AI to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photographs, and research family relationships to make their schemes more convincing. Authorities recommend establishing code words with family members, verifying urgent requests through known contacts, and avoiding immediate responses to unexpected calls or messages requesting money.
